The Prote{{ls}}tants of our time (as vve may {{ls}}ee in al Countries vvhere the {{ls}}ecular {{ls}}word is dravven again{{ls}}t their Sectes) care neither for the one nor for the other, though they extol onely the {{ls}}ecular vvhen it maketh for them. {{outside L|The obedience of Catholikes both to Spiritual and temporal Superiors.}}The Catholikes onely mo{{ls}}t humbly obey both, euen according to Gods ordinance, the one in temporal cau{{ls}}es, and the other in Spiritual: in vvhich order both the{{ls}}e States haue ble{{ls}}{{ls}}edly flori{{ls}}hed in al Chri{{ls}}tian countries euer {{ls}}ince Chri{{ls}}tes time, and it is the very vvay to pre{{ls}}erue both, as one day al the world {{ls}}hal confe{{ls}}{{ls}}e vvith vs.

You giue tributes.''] Though euery man ought to be ready to {{ls}}erue his temporal Prince vvith his goods, by tributes or vvhat other lavvful taxes and {{ls}}ub{{ls}}idies {{ls}}o euer: {{outside R|''Hiero. in Mat. 17''.}}yet they may exempt by priuileges vvhom they thinke good. {{outside L|The Clergie exempted from tribute.}}As in al countries Chri{{ls}}tian: Prie{{ls}}ts for the honour of Chri{{ls}}t, who{{ls}}e Mini{{ls}}ters they be, haue by the grauntes and auncient charters of kings bene excepted and exempted.
